note: Configuration Provider defines a ConfigProvider plugin type (Plugin/ConfigProvider, manager plugin.manager.config_provider.processor, annotation @ConfigProvider, base ConfigProviderBase) and two shipped plugins: config/install (weight -10) and config/optional (weight 10). The config_provider.collector service (ConfigCollector::addInstallableConfig($extensions)) runs all providers and writes the union of provided config into config_provider.storage (a core MemoryStorage, request-scoped). It also decorates core config.installer. No configure route, no permissions, no Drush, no config entity of its own. Medium cases require running the live collector service for a real enabled module (deterministic real output: node -> node.settings + views/actions; user -> user.settings + user.role.* ). Hard cases require the agent to collect a module's installable config via config_provider and store the resulting config names in Drupal State, verified against live State.

evals.prompt: The Drupal contrib module config_provider defines a ConfigProvider plugin type and ships two default plugins that mirror core's install storages. What are the two plugins (their ids / directories)?
evals.expected_output: It ships ConfigProviderInstall with id config/install (weight -10) and ConfigProviderOptional with id config/optional (weight 10), corresponding to an extension's config/install and config/optional directories.

evals.prompt: Programmatically, how do you use config_provider to find out what configuration is installable for the enabled extensions? Name the service, the method, and where the collected result is stored.
evals.expected_output: Call \Drupal::service('config_provider.collector')->addInstallableConfig() (optionally passing an Extension array to limit it). It runs every provider plugin and writes the union into the config_provider.storage service, a core MemoryStorage you then read with listAll()/read().

evals.prompt: How do you add a custom configuration provider to config_provider? Name the base class, the annotation, and the main method you implement.
evals.expected_output: Create a plugin class under src/Plugin/ConfigProvider/ extending ConfigProviderBase with a @ConfigProvider annotation (id/weight/label), and implement addInstallableConfig() to write provided config into $this->providerStorage (addConfigToCreate() is often a no-op).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the config_provider collector to find out what configuration the node module provides for installation. Name one specific configuration object it collects for node.
evals.expected_output: Run \Drupal::service('config_provider.collector')->addInstallableConfig(['node' => \Drupal::service('extension.list.module')->get('node')]) then read config_provider.storage->listAll(); it includes node.settings, the node view modes (e.g. core.entity_view_mode.node.teaser), node system actions, and views such as views.view.content and views.view.frontpage.

evals.prompt: Using config_provider on this live site, determine the configuration the user module provides. Name a config object among the user roles or settings that the collector reports for the user module.
evals.expected_output: Collecting for the user module (config_provider.collector->addInstallableConfig(['user' => ...])) yields user.settings, user.mail, user.flood, and the roles user.role.anonymous and user.role.authenticated (plus user view modes, actions and views).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use config_provider's collector service to collect the installable configuration for the node module, then store the resulting list of configuration object names (an array) into Drupal State under the key 'config_provider_eval_node'. Apply this to the live site.
evals.expected_output: e.g. drush php:eval: $c=\Drupal::service('config_provider.collector'); $c->addInstallableConfig(['node'=>\Drupal::service('extension.list.module')->get('node')]); \Drupal::state()->set('config_provider_eval_node', \Drupal::service('config_provider.storage')->listAll()); — the stored array must include node.settings.

evals.prompt: Using config_provider, collect the installable configuration for the user module on this site and save the array of collected config object names into Drupal State under the key 'config_provider_eval_user'. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Collect for the user module via config_provider.collector->addInstallableConfig(['user'=>...]) and store config_provider.storage->listAll() into state key config_provider_eval_user; the stored array must include user.role.authenticated (and user.settings).
